2.4.12.summary: ChartFox charts in the EFB and on the map, an accurate landing rate, terminals and gates at airports, and new airport and aircraft icons.

features: Connect your ChartFox account in Charts: its charts lead the chart list by type and open in the Stratos viewer.
Your route's georeferenced ChartFox SID, STAR and approach are laid on the map automatically; turn them off with the ChartFox chip in Layers.
Airport terminals now appear on the airport map.
improvements: Landing rate comes from the simulator's own touchdown and wheel contact, not the flare. Restart the bridge to use it.
SIDs and STARs are named by their procedure, e.g. SID - OSHNN5.
Many more traffic aircraft show their real shape instead of a generic plane.
fixes: Charts no longer shows the previous airport's country and publisher after switching airports.
Gates are visible on the airport map at normal zoom.
ui: Airports are shown as pins, with major airports in purple.
A new Charts icon, and a tidier Charts layout.

2.4.11.summary: Automatic aircraft photography: the EFB finds a photo of the exact aircraft you are flying, with clearly labelled stand-ins when it cannot.

features: Automatic aircraft photos in the EFB flight widget, by registration from X-Plane or MSFS, with the photographer's credit and a link to Planespotters.
When the exact aircraft has no photo: the aircraft flying your flight today, the same airline and type, the same type, or an illustration, each clearly labelled.
Find image retries the search, and Set reg adds a backup registration.
improvements: MSFS now reports the aircraft type and airline; X-Plane follows a switch to another aircraft.
Photo lookups are cached, spaced out and retried, so they never slow the simulator.

2.4.10.summary: A new EFB home screen: a flight tracking widget with the aircraft's photo, departure and arrival clocks, and apps and widgets you can put anywhere.

features: Flight tracking widget: the aircraft's photo by registration, callsign, route, scheduled and estimated times, progress, altitude, speed and phase.
Departure and arrival clock widgets with each airport's local time from your SimBrief plan.
Hold the home screen to edit it: drag apps and widgets anywhere, move apps in and out of the dock, and add or remove widgets.
improvements: Re-import your SimBrief plan once so the airport clocks can show local time.

2.4.9.summary: A lock screen and home bar for the EFB, the Flight Deck map inside Navigator, and a quieter phone map.

features: The EFB opens on a lock screen over its own wallpaper, with the airline's logo behind it: the time, UTC and local clocks, your flight, the simulator connection and a calendar. Swipe up to open it.
A home bar on the EFB home screen: swipe it up to return to the Flight Deck.
Navigator now shows the Flight Deck map itself, with every layer and control.
improvements: The lock screen follows your finger and settles with the same motion as an iPad.
fixes: The Stratos wing on the EFB home screen no longer shows a faint square around it.
ui: On a phone, the telemetry strip and the aircraft card open when you tap an aircraft instead of staying on screen.

2.4.8.summary: Prepar3D and FSX support, X-Plane 11 navigation data, and a map that wraps around the world without a black edge.

features: Prepar3D v4 to v6: Stratos finds Prepar3D's own SimConnect library and connects to it automatically.
FSX: tried through the same SimConnect connection. FSX is 32-bit, so this depends on it accepting the 64-bit connection.
X-Plane 11: the bridge now finds X-Plane 11 installs for SIDs, STARs, ILS and the IFR charts, as it does for X-Plane 12.
improvements: Settings shows which simulator SimConnect is connected to: MSFS, Prepar3D or FSX.
fixes: Zooming out or panning past the date line no longer leaves a black side: map tiles, radar and FAA charts repeat around the world.
Aircraft, airports, the route and your own aircraft repeat on every visible copy of the world, and clicking a copy selects the real one.
X-Plane 11 ILS courses show the true course instead of a wrong 360° magnetic.
ui: The top-bar Go Premium button is gone. Stratos is free, and a Support Stratos button appears only when a support page is set.

2.2.1.summary: Route Finder, a new EFB app: real flights in the air now, filtered by aircraft, airline and flight time, each ready to uplink to SimBrief. The EFB home screen now shows the Stratos wing.

features: Route Finder: real airline flights in the air now, with callsign, departure, arrival, distance and estimated block time.
Filter by aircraft type, airline and flight time, from under an hour to over eight.
Uplink to SimBrief opens the flight planner prefilled with the airline, flight number, aircraft and both airports.
ui: The EFB home screen shows the Stratos wing as its default wallpaper; an airline's logo still replaces it when one is set.

2.2.0.summary: IFR en-route charts, a jet-stream and turbulence map with legends, SIGMETs, holding points and an ILS card, smoother live tracking, and a pro chart workspace with pinned charts, night mode, split view and Auto.

features: IFR Low and IFR High charts on the Flight Deck map and in the Flight Planner: airways with minimum altitudes, Class B/C/D and restricted airspace, and grid MORA, read from X-Plane 12 through the bridge.
Jet stream layer: upper-level wind speed at a chosen flight level (FL180 to FL450) with isotachs, from Open-Meteo.
Turbulence layer: the Ellrod clear-air turbulence index between two flight levels, outlined light, moderate and severe.
SIGMETs and US G-AIRMETs from NOAA: a map layer, and a card in the EFB weather page filtered to the route or station.
Holding points on the EFB ground chart, with the holds on the taxi route listed.
ILS and localizer card on the EFB airport page: frequency, course, glide slope and DME from X-Plane 12.
Chart clipboard, night rendering, split view with a moving map, and Auto chart selection by flight phase.
improvements: The aircraft moves smoothly between position updates on every live map, phone included.
Rain radar uses RainViewer's sharper 512 px tiles up to its zoom limit, with a legend for every weather layer.
With the bridge offline, airport procedures fall back to the bundled FAA data and the ground chart reads OpenStreetMap directly.
The bridge tries several OpenStreetMap servers when one is down.
US airports show FAA charts again when no Airmate licence is configured.
One shared colour and type system for the Flight Deck, the EFB and phones.
Shorter on-screen text, frequencies as 118.300 and three-digit headings.
fixes: The EFB airport page showed no published procedures for every airport.
Opening another airport in the EFB by link did not reload the page.
SIGMET areas crossing the 180 degree meridian were drawn across the whole map.
Airway endpoints could not be matched because fixes stored the wrong region.
ui: On phones, one panel opens at a time and the map starts clear.
Taxiways on the ground chart are drawn as yellow centrelines.

2.1.45.summary: A chart on the map can now be placed with two snapped clicks, then moved, turned and sized by hand. Charts are drawn in their own page scale and re-rendered sharper as you enlarge them, and Airmate joins as a source with the georeferencing it publishes.

features: Align takes two clicks: the chart click snaps to the end of a drawn runway band, the map click to a published threshold, so the pair names the runway ends that placed the sheet.
One lock replaces the eight nudge arrows: unlocked, drag moves the chart, Shift-drag turns it and Alt-drag sizes it, one screen pixel following the pointer at any zoom.
Turn and Size sliders set the same corrections to a tenth of a degree and a percent, from 1% to 400%, saved with the placement.
Airmate joins as a chart source: the catalogue is fetched server-side with the licence key, documents are proxied, and its georeferencing places a plate from metadata alone.
Charts are measured in the page own points and rendered again at the resolution the screen asks for, so an enlarged plate stays sharp instead of magnifying its pixels.
improvements: US charts come from the licensed Airmate source; the FAA d-TPP sheets are no longer offered beside it.
Unlicensed, a US airport names the source its charts need instead of showing a second-best plate.
The catalogue no longer lets the browser HTTP cache answer with a source that has since changed hands.
A stored placement survives a change of render resolution, because its points are kept in page coordinates.
fixes: Dragging a chart at a size other than 100% moved it a fraction of the distance the pointer did.
Chart labels are anchored at their printed centre and grouped along their own direction, which brought a STAR label fit from 1.6 km to 0.6 km of residual.
other: Includes the in-cycle work on anchoring the estimated field and the VATSIM ATC layer.

2.1.44.summary: The logbook can now import a flight history from Volanta or ELEVATEX, matching columns by meaning and leaving everything the export does not state empty.

features: Settings → Data gains Import Volanta / ELEVATEX, which reads a Volanta CSV or JSON export, or the flights.csv from an ELEVATEX export, and merges the flights into the local logbook.
improvements: Re-importing the same export updates the records it already wrote instead of duplicating them, because every imported flight gets a stable id from its route and departure time.
Columns are matched by meaning, so the two exports' different headers, day-first dates and clock, minute or hours-and-minutes durations are all read correctly.
ui: The import sits beside the existing backup controls and reports how many flights were added and how many are in the logbook afterwards.
compatibility: Only what the export states is imported: landing rate, altitude and track stay empty and the logbook shows them as not measured.

2.1.43.summary: The flat map keeps only the six base styles it can really paint, FAA VFR and IFR charts load at the level that carries chart data when zoomed out, satellite imagery works in local development, and the side-panel toggle is gone.

improvements: Chart tiles are fetched one level above the current view, so VFR, Low IFR and High IFR gain detail as the map is zoomed in instead of staying at a coarse overview.
fixes: FAA VFR, Low IFR and High IFR charts no longer request blank overview tiles when the map is slightly zoomed out; each layer starts at the level that actually carries chart data.
Satellite imagery loads again in local development: the dev server answers the /tile/ request the page makes over http instead of returning 404.
ui: The flat map offers six base styles: Satellite, Terrain, World, VFR, Low IFR and High IFR. Basic, Detailed, Light, Dark and Hybrid are retired, and a saved style that no longer exists falls back to Satellite.
The remove-side-panels control is gone from the map, along with the layout state it saved.

2.1.42.summary: Live traffic labels now show both the callsign and the aircraft type, so a target is identifiable without opening its card.

features: The 2D map and 3D globe labels now show callsign, aircraft type and altitude or flight level together.
improvements: The selected aircraft and own-ship marker show the same callsign and type, with the type normalised to an ICAO code.
ui: Longer 3D labels are width-limited and ellipsized instead of running off the map.

2.1.41.summary: Selected traffic now has a real 3D altitude path on the Flight Deck globe, with detailed type artwork at the top, a ground shadow beneath, and the live callsign and flight level attached to the aircraft.

features: The selected aircraft's recorded trail now rises from the ground as a translucent 3D altitude curtain, with an altitude-coloured top edge and a faint ground trace.
The selected aircraft rides at the top of that path as its detailed type silhouette, turned to its live heading with a callsign and flight-level badge.
The aircraft's surface position remains a subdued detailed shadow inside an amber anchor ring, joined to the airborne marker by a dashed stalk.
Traffic now uses the detailed aircraft artwork from the chart atlas, with a neutral detailed fallback for types that have no dedicated sprite.
improvements: The selected path includes the aircraft's current position and altitude, so the 3D marker sits on the live target instead of stopping at the last polled sample.
The ground shadow suppresses its own map label, leaving one callsign on the airborne marker and no duplicate target below.
The marker, badge and altitude curtain follow the same camera as the globe through pitch, rotation and zoom.
fixes: Selected traffic no longer leaves the callsign and aircraft on the ground while its recorded path is elevated; the airborne marker and ground anchor now separate the two.
Aircraft types missing from the sprite atlas now use the detailed neutral silhouette rather than the simple legacy shape.
performance: Traffic icons are cached per aircraft type, and the selected 3D path is redrawn only when the camera or selected samples change.
ui: The 3D path uses the existing instrument palette: cyan and amber rings, an altitude-coloured edge, and a compact callsign and flight-level badge.
compatibility: The 3D path is built only from observed traffic samples; a filed route remains a flat planned line because it carries no observed altitude profile.

2.2.2.summary: Route Finder now finds any real airline flight, not just those airborne, with airport filters and a flight-time slider. Desktop updates now prompt on launch and install inside the app.

features: Route Finder searches every known real airline route; FLYING NOW limits it to flights airborne right now.
Route Finder filters by departure and arrival airport.
improvements: Flight time is a slider from 30 minutes to 21 hours.
On Windows, Update Now downloads the new version, checks its published checksum, installs it and reopens Stratos.
fixes: The desktop app now detects new releases: it read the version file packaged with itself and always thought it was current.
ui: Removed the DIRECT TO button from the EFB and Flight Deck, and the TRK button from the Flight Deck.
compatibility: Installs of 2.2.1 or older must update to 2.2.2 by hand once; later updates are offered in the app.

2.2.3.summary: Route Finder shows the aircraft type for every flight.

features: Every Route Finder flight shows its aircraft type: the exact one when that flight was seen in today’s live traffic, otherwise the airline’s typical type for the distance, marked TYPICAL.
improvements: Choosing an aircraft in Route Finder skips flights seen today on a different type.

2.2.4.summary: A new performance calculator: V1/VR/V2, FLEX and flaps for takeoff, VAPP, autobrake and stopping point for landing, drawn on a to-scale runway. Weight & Balance uplinks its weights to it.

features: Performance: takeoff speeds, FLEX or assumed temperature and the best flap setting; landing VAPP, autobrake and stopping distance with the 1.15 factor.
A to-scale runway diagram with V1 and VR, the 35 ft and stop flags, the stopping distance and the runway margin.
Weight & Balance can uplink its takeoff and landing weights to Performance.
improvements: Performance profiles for the A319, A320, A320neo, A330-900, A350-900, A380, 737-800, 737 MAX 8 and 787-9.
Results update as you type, with a wind compass, weight gauge and density altitude.
other: Speeds and distances are Stratos estimates for simulator use, not certified performance.

2.2.5.summary: A new graphite look across Stratos and an iPadOS-style EFB home screen with flight and clock widgets.

features: EFB home: an iPadOS-style layout with glass widgets for the flight and a UTC clock beside the app grid, and a frosted dock.
improvements: A graphite night theme across the EFB, Flight Deck and Profile pages: neutral surfaces, one blue accent, a magenta route and tighter corners.
The Settings colour board documents the new palette.
fixes: The phone flight panel no longer shows the heading with a doubled degree sign.
The A320 checklist no longer says Stratos does not compute performance.

2.2.6.summary: SID and STAR procedures load worldwide in the desktop app, and the website deploys again with the current installer.

fixes: The desktop app draws SIDs, STARs and approaches for every airport in your X-Plane data: procedure requests now reach the Stratos bridge directly.
The website deploys again and its download buttons serve the current installer; it had stopped updating at 2.1.45.

2.2.7.summary: A rebuilt Flight Planner: click the chart to draw the route, a DEP / route / ARR bar, a legs table and waypoints across the whole chart.

features: Flight Planner: every chart click adds the waypoint under it and draws the leg; the first click picks the departure airport.
A route bar with DEP, the route as text and ARR. Type fixes or coordinates and press Enter; unknown idents are named, not guessed.
A legs table with the route, track, leg distance and running total for every point.
improvements: Waypoints from the simulator data now cover the whole chart: the new Fit view radius follows the zoom, and fixes are hidden only when zoomed far out.
The planner is four tabs (Route, Procedures, Fuel, Review) instead of a six-step wizard, and the planned route is drawn in magenta.
fixes: Planned route lines were not drawn on the EFB maps since 2.2.0; the Flight Planner and the Navigator show them again.
The Flight Planner chart no longer freezes for most of a second each time it is panned or zoomed.
Reopening the Flight Planner starts the chart at the plan instead of the default map.

2.2.8.summary: MSFS 2020 and 2024 tracking works in the desktop app.

fixes: MSFS 2020 and 2024 are tracked again: the desktop app now ships the SimConnect connector it needs, which earlier builds left out.
The bridge no longer tells desktop users to run pip install SimConnect; the connector comes with the app.

2.2.9.summary: Website downloads always lead to an installer, and search results go to the Stratos homepage.

improvements: Searching for Stratos now leads to the homepage instead of inner app pages or an old preview address.
fixes: The website's macOS download links work again: when a release has no build for a platform, the newest one that does is offered.

2.3.0.summary: Route Finder shows the real stand a parked aircraft is at, so you can start your flight from the same gate.

features: Route Finder (Flying now): an aircraft parked at its departure or arrival airport shows its real stand or gate, matched from its live position to the stands charted in OpenStreetMap.
improvements: Flying now results say whether a flight is at the gate, has arrived, is taxiing or is airborne.

2.3.1.summary: Stratos on Chromebook: install it from Chrome and follow your flight from the PC.

features: ChromeOS: the website explains how to install Stratos on a Chromebook from Chrome and follow your flight from the PC running the simulator.

2.4.0.summary: Charts on the map with a search bar, UAE charts, IVAO traffic, airport weather, FAA chart layers and a cleaner World map.

features: Charts on the map: a new Charts button in Map settings → Layers opens one panel with a search bar. Pick a STAR, SID or approach and it is laid over the map in the right place, with an opacity slider.
UAE charts: Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah and Al Maktoum charts from the GCAA, shown inside Stratos.
IVAO traffic: choose IVAO as the traffic source to see live IVAO pilots on the map.
Airport weather layer: every reporting station in view, coloured by flight category, with wind, visibility, ceiling and temperature as you zoom in.
US chart layers: FAA Sectional, Terminal, IFR Low and IFR High charts as map layers.
improvements: The desktop app can now open charts outside the US.
fixes: Phone mode: the EFB dock no longer covers the app icons, Settings titles use the full width, and the Flight Plan chart card no longer hides half the map.
ui: The World map has a cleaner chart style in night and day: muted water, plain land, crisp coastlines, quiet borders and a light grid.

2.4.1.summary: Watch your flight in 3D: real 3D aircraft models, a chase camera that follows your plane, and a live Status line.

features: 3D chase view: a new 3D chase button in Map settings puts the camera behind your aircraft at its real altitude, looking along its track over satellite imagery and terrain.
3D aircraft models: your plane and traffic fly as 3D aircraft at their real altitude, heading and bank, with a line down to the ground.
Realistic models for A320s, A321s and widebodies; jumbos, regional jets, turboprops, business jets and light aircraft get their own shapes.
Airline colours: popular airlines such as Emirates, Lufthansa, British Airways, Delta, Ryanair, easyJet and KLM are painted in their colours (no logos) on the shapes drawn in code.
Your own A320 is drawn with a detailed model in the 3D views.
Status line: the live strip now says what the flight is doing, for example "Climbing through 12,300 ft · 2,950 NM to EGLL" or "Final approach into EGLL".
improvements: The 3D views show a daylight sky and haze at the horizon instead of black.
fixes: The aircraft symbol on the 3D map points along its heading when the map is rotated.
other: 3D aircraft models are credited on the map and in SOURCES_AND_LICENSING.md (CC BY 4.0, Sketchfab).

2.4.2.summary: Tracking a flight in 3D now follows the 3D aircraft itself, with its trail drawn at real altitude.

improvements: Following a selected flight in the 3D views keeps the aircraft itself in the middle of the screen, at its altitude.
fixes: 3D views: the selected flight no longer shows a yellow ground ring and a flat orange icon beside its 3D model.
3D views: the selected flight's trail is drawn in 3D at its recorded altitude and ends at the aircraft model.

2.4.3.summary: The 3D views go back to the aircraft symbol on its altitude stalk; the 3D aircraft models are removed.

improvements: The 3D chase view follows your aircraft symbol on its altitude stalk again.
performance: The 3D aircraft models are removed, making the app about 18 MB smaller and the 3D views lighter.
ui: 3D views: aircraft are drawn as symbols again, with the selected flight's altitude trail.

2.4.4.summary: EFB map displays: VFR, low and high IFR maps with real airspace, a taxi route you click on the ground chart, a flight and airport search with Go to, and a cleaner Flight Deck.

features: Map displays: VFR, IFR Low and IFR High vector maps, with terrain, airways and labels drawn for pilots.
Airspaces layer: controlled and special-use airspace from FAA data and your simulator, with class and altitude limits.
Taxi route: turn it on, click taxiways on the ground chart, and a green guide line follows the taxiways, listing them in order.
Search flights, airports and navaids from the Flight Deck; Go to takes the map there and tracks a flight, even one elsewhere on the network.
EFB airport ground chart: a Find taxiway search highlights a taxiway and zooms to it.
improvements: Your aircraft is a magenta arrowhead pointing along your track; the aircraft icon is still available in Settings.
The route draws as a cased line with boxed ident tags, leg distance and track labels, and chart symbols for each point.
Ground charts use chart colours, show stand numbers and name each taxiway once.
Navaids use enroute chart colours on every map: blue VORs (boxed with DME), purple NDBs, grey fixes and teal airports.
3D views place the trail and altitude stalk at the aircraft's exact height.
fixes: The EFB airport ground chart no longer stays on Loading: it reads the map tiles first and adds the bridge's data when it arrives.
Taxiway labels no longer keep a leading Taxiway or Twy.
ui: The Flight Deck map runs to the top edge: the top bar is replaced by a search panel at the top left.
Map settings are grouped into Map, Weather, Aeronautical and Traffic sections.
Shared fonts, spacing and top bar across the Live, Logbook and Weather pages.

2.4.5.summary: A phone layout built for the cockpit: map tools in one rail, your departure and arrival charts one tap away, and a cleaner map.

features: Phone Flight Deck: a tray above the tab bar pins your departure and arrival airports with their charts, plus a Sync with flight switch.
improvements: Phone Flight Deck: the map tools sit in one rail on the left, with search opening beside it on demand.
Phone tab bar: Map, Plan, Flights, Charts and More, so every label has room; More holds the EFB apps, Airports, Weather and Profile.
Phone map labels no longer pile up: a label without room is left out, and navaids appear one zoom step later.
The EFB flight planner on a phone shows airports and your route when zoomed out, adding navaids and fixes as you zoom in.
fixes: Phone: the Flight Deck search no longer runs under the map buttons.
Phone: the EFB home dock no longer covers the last row of apps.
ui: Phone: the floating Plan button and the empty flight plan and procedures cards are gone from the map; the Plan tab opens the planner.

2.4.6.summary: Phones always open the phone layout, including after visiting the EFB, and the download panel is gone from the map.

improvements: Phone: the Status panel sits just above the charts tray, and the map credit moves to the top right.
fixes: Phone: coming back to the map from the EFB, a new tab or a relaunched app no longer shows the older layout.
Phone: the phone layout is detected correctly on first load; the page set its width before the viewport was known.
ui: The Download Stratos panel is removed from the Flight Deck map.

2.4.7.summary: A thicker route line on the Flight Deck map, easier to follow over dark water and satellite imagery.

ui: The planned route is drawn twice as thick (a 12 px line over an 18 px outline), and the part already flown widens to match.
